summary: Provisioned Dell XPS 13 (9310) resumes from hibernate to black screen; Intel Ethernet driver rebind loop
description:
Issue summary:
Several newly provisioned Dell XPS 13 (9310) units in the corp provisioning lab fail to resume from hibernate (S4). Machines appear to power on (fans/charging LED) but the display remains black and user input is unresponsive. After ~30–90s some devices show recurring Network driver resets and kernel/driver rebind logs, which correlate with the black screen condition.

Impact:
- Blocks completion of automated provisioning validation (image QA jobs) for affected XPS devices.
- Prevents new devices from being handed off to employees until a manual power-cycle and driver rollback are applied.
- Affects ~6 of 24 test devices in the lab; intermittent across firmware revisions.

Environment:
- Image: windows-image-2026-03 (corporate build, Win11 23H2-based)
- Lab: corp-provisioning-lab, us-west rack A3
- Device model: Dell XPS 13 9310 (i7, Intel Ethernet via USB-C adapter on test bench)
- Drivers: Intel Ethernet driver package intel-net-26.3.0.1 (shipped in image), Dell BIOS 1.14.0

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Flash windows-image-2026-03 to XPS 9310 test unit via provisioning rig.
2) Apply corporate policies and restart; initiate hibernate (S4) via powercfg /hibernate on + shutdown /h.
3) Resume via power button.
4) System fans spin, charging LED on, but display stays black and no input accepted.
5) Watch provisioning rig console: repeated EventLog entries where e1qexpress (Intel) reports "Device Reset/Link lost" then driver rebind attempts.

Logs & artifacts:
- Collected full WindowsEvent log extract (attached in imaging artifacts folder): Event IDs 7026, 219, and repeated kernel-driver unload/load timestamps clustered at resume time.
- Photos of external console showing black screen and probe outputs available in /shared/internal-support/INT-714159/artifacts.
- Live kernel-mode dump captured on one unit (small memory dump) and uploaded to imaging bucket.

Notes on reproducibility:
- Issue is intermittent but reliably triggered on some firmware/driver combos. Not all XPS 9310 units repro. Units that were updated to BIOS 1.14.0 + intel-net-26.3.0.1 show higher frequency.

Immediate impact classification: workstation provisioning blocker for a subset of XPS models in lab.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypotheses:
- Power-management interaction between Intel Ethernet driver and Windows resume path causing a DPC/block that prevents graphics driver init.
- Race between USB-C/Thunderbolt controller resume and display driver initialization on these units.

Actions taken so far:
- Reproduced on 6/24 lab units. Captured event logs and small memory dump.
- Rolled back intel-net driver to intel-net-25.8.0.0 on one repro unit: resume succeeded and no black screen observed across 5 repeated tests.
- Swapped to Dell BIOS 1.13.2 on one unit: repro rate dropped significantly.
- Verified not related to BitLocker (BitLocker not yet enabled during image validation).
- Eng (kernel/drivers team) performed static analysis of dump; noted blocked worker thread waiting on NIC driver completion during init.

Open questions:
- Is the issue specific to the intel-net 26.3.0.1 package we recently added to image?
- Are the USB-C NICs being enumerated as late devices causing display init to stall?

Data points & links:
- Imaging CI job logs: https://ci.internal.redwood/imaging/1234 (last failing run attached)
- Dump and log bundle: s3://redwood-internal/INT-714159/dumps.zip
- See linked: INT-41256 (wake-from-lid issues) which had a similar driver / resume pattern.
resolution:
Workaround (short-term):
- For staging/provisioning lab: pin intel-net driver to intel-net-25.8.0.0 in the imaging package. Update provisioning rig orchestration to apply driver rollback step when model == XPS_9310 until a formal fix is released.
- Instruct bench techs to perform a full AC disconnect + power-button hold (10s) as a manual recovery for units in the field.

Planned permanent fix:
- Drivers team to produce a patched intel-net package that defers certain power-management completion paths on resume (PR referenced below).
- Imaging to build a new windows-image-2026-03.1 with the patched driver + optional suspend/resume stress test in CI.
- Coordinate with Dell to validate BIOS behavior; if required, mark older BIOS 1.13.2 as recommended for provisioning until firmware fix is available.

Follow-ups / next steps:
- Drivers team to ship a candidate driver and open PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/drivers/pull/1034 (in progress).
- Imaging to run full lab validation and confirm fix by 2026-03-17.
- Create advisory for bench SOP: "If XPS 9310 fails resume, apply driver rollback and escalate to imaging team".

Status: In Progress — workaround in place in provisioning lab; pending driver patch and image rebuild.
